headline: The Eisenstein fibration is one member of the Springer regular-element tower of W(E8), not a unique object. Every divisor d of a degree gives a regular centraliser of order equal to the product of the degrees divisible by d. What distinguishes d = 3 is measured here rather than assumed.
law: |C_W(regular w of order d)| = product of the degrees of W divisible by d (Springer). Degrees of W(E8): 2,8,12,14,18,20,24,30.
reading: 'q = 3 is forced' is a claim about this tower and is now testable rather than asserted. d = 4 supplies a rank-4 Gaussian sibling (Shephard-Todd G31, order 46080 = 8*12*20*24), so the mere existence of a rank-4 complex-reflection centraliser does not single out the Eisenstein case. Whatever distinguishes d = 3 has to be read off the columns here -- transitivity of the derived subgroup and the block structure -- not from the existence of the centraliser.
scope: Structural census of the tower. It does not claim d = 3 is or is not distinguished; it supplies the table on which that claim must be settled.
